sentences.text: Author: Lalitha Kanneganti
Bench: Lalitha Kanneganti  THE HONOURABLE SMT JUSTICE LALITHA KANNEGANTI  M.A.C.M.A.No.1741 of 2006  and  M.A. C.M.A.No.833 of 2023 COMMON JUDGMENT:
Since both these appeals arise out of the same award, they are being disposed of by this common judgment.

2. M.A.C.M.A.No.1741 of 2006 is preferred by the United India Insurance Company Limited and M.A.C.M.A.No.833 of 2023 is preferred by the National Insurance Company Limited aggrieved by the award and decree dated 08-05-2006 in O.P.No.46 of 2005 on the file of the Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Jude, Karimangar at Jagtial, questioning the liability fastened against them.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Jude, Karimangar at Jagtial
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Heard learned counsel for the appellant-United India Insurance Company Mr. Vutla Srinivasa Rao and learned counsel for the respondents-claimants Mr. V. Jithender Rao in M.A.C.M.A.No.1741 of 2006 and learned counsel for the appellant-National Insurance Company Limited Mr. Kota Subba Rao and learned counsel for respondent No.8-Mr. Vutla Srinivasa Rao in M.A.C.M.A.No.833 of 2023.
Perused the record.

4. The brief facts are that on 03-12-2004 at 5-00 PM., while the deceased Bairi Vijaya along with her husband and relatives were 2 LK, J M.A.C.M.A.No.1741 of 2006 and M.A.C.M.A. No.833 of 2023 returning from the temple in an auto bearing No.AP-25-U-1183 and at about 6-15 PM., when the auto reached near Vishwa Bharathi Model School at Koratla, a jeep bearing No.MH-12-J-0729 came in opposite direction, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner at high speed and dashed against the auto, due to which the auto turned turtle and all the inmates have received injuries and on the way to the hospital, the deceased died.
The claimants being husband and children of the deceased have filed OP., claiming compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- for the death of the deceased in the accident.

5. The owner of jeep has filed counter denying the manner of accident and stated that the driver of auto drove the same in a zigzag manner and in a rash and negligent manner and he was responsible for the accident, but not the driver of jeep.

sentences.text: The Insurance Company of jeep filed counter denying the manner of accident and the negligence attributed to the driver of jeep.
It is stated that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of auto and since there is a collision, the owner and insurer of the auto are liable to pay compensation.

7. The driver and the owner of auto have filed different counters with identical allegations stating that the driver of auto was driving very slowly and the police also registered a case against the jeep driver and 3 LK, J M.A.C.M.A.No.1741 of 2006 and M.A.C.M.A. No.833 of 2023 the charge sheet was filed against him and the negligence of the driver of auto was not established.
8. The Insurance Company of auto filed counter stating that the driver of auto is no way responsible for the accident.
He denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased and the claim is highly excessive.

9. The Tribunal, on analyzing the oral and documentary evidence and relying on the judgment of this Court in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs. K. Anjaiah and others1, held that there was contributory negligence on the part of the driver of auto and apportioned the contributory negligence at 20% on the auto and 80% on the jeep and awarded compensation of Rs.2,65,500/-
with interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Aggrieved by the same,
both the Insurances Companies have filed the present appeals.

10. Learned counsel for the appellant-United India Insurance Company Limited i.e, the insurer of auto, submits that as per the evidence on record, the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the jeep and as such there is no contributory negligence on the part of the driver of auto.

. Learned counsel for the appellant-National Insurance Company i.e., the insurer of the jeep, has relied on the judgment of this Court in New India Assurance Company Limited, Hyderabad Vs.
S.V.Balakishna and others 2 wherein this Court held that under Section 92-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, all the owners of the vehicles involved in the accident are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation on the principle of "no fault liability".

entities.text:
New India Assurance Company Limited, Hyderabad Vs.
S.V.Balakishna and others 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said referred case, both the lorry and the APSRTC bus were involved in the accident and both were held jointly and severally liable to pay Rs.7,500/- compensation under "no fault liability' to the claimant.
Relying on the said judgment, he submits that the accident has happened in the year 2004 and as no fault liability was Rs.50,000/-, both the vehicles have to pay Rs.25,000/- each.
12. This Court having heard the learned counsels on either side has perused the entire material on record.

The entire evidence on record reveals that the accident has happened due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of jeep and the crime was registered and the charge sheet was filed against the driver of jeep.
Even as per the charge sheet, nothing has been elicited that there was contributory negligence on the part of the driver of auto.

Just because a person was sitting besides the driver, that itself cannot be a ground for the 1997(2) ALT 386 (S.B.) 5 LK, J M.A.C.M.A.No.1741 of 2006 and M.A.C.M.A. No.833 of 2023 Court to presume that there was contributory negligence The United India Insruance Co Ltd vs Bairi Narayana And 7 Ors on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183040935/
2 on the part of the driver of the auto.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Without there being any evidence and even though the insurer of the jeep has not discharged the burden caste upon them to show that there was contributory negligence on the part of the auto, the Tribunal has apportioned the negligence at 20% on the part of the auto driver and 80% on the part of the jeep driver.

In the considered opinion of this Court, the said finding is without any basis and the accident has happened due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the jeep and there is no contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the auto.

13. However, in the light of the law laid down by this Court in S.V.Balakishna's case (cited 2 supra),
when two vehicles are involved in the accident, under 'no fault liability', both the vehicles have to pay half of the compensation.
As the accident occurred in the year 2004, it is stated that 'no fault liability' was at Rs.50,000/-, as such, both the vehicles have to pay a sum of Rs.25,000/- each.
The Tribunal, after considering the entire evidence on record, has granted compensation of Rs.2,65,500/-.

In that, the United India Insurance Company i.e., the insurer of auto, is liable to pay an amount of Rs.25,000/- and the remaining amount of Rs.2,40,500/- is liable to be paid by the National Insurance Company Limited i.e., the insurer of jeep.
6 LK, J M.A.C.M.A.No.1741 of 2006 and M.A.C.M.A. No.833 of 2023 14.
Accordingly, the appeals are partly allowed.
No order as to costs.
15. Miscellaneous petitions, if any pending in both the appeals shall stand closed.
_ __ SMT LALITHA KANNEGANTI, J 21st June, 2023.
